hints.S52_A1: The farm is compared to a LIBRARY, and NOT A SINGLE ANIMAL HAD WOKEN UP. Ask: does a library feel loud, busy or dark, or does it feel like silence itself? Match the adjective to the library.
hints.S52_A2: The STORM is coming, and the children must leave for the MARKET IMMEDIATELY. Ask: which phrasal verb means to begin a journey? 'Return' means to come back, and 'wait' would keep them exactly where they are.
hints.S52_A3: The soil must end up LOOSE AND RICH, and the work is done BEFORE PLANTING THE SEEDS. Ask: which verb means to turn the earth over and prepare it? 'Watered' only adds water; 'painted' belongs to walls.
hints.S52_A4: The goats are EATING GRASS and WANDERING WHEREVER THEY PLEASED in the MEADOW. Ask: which verb describes an animal feeding slowly on grass as it moves about? 'Sleeping' and 'hiding' involve no eating at all.
hints.S52_A5: The clue follows the dash: EVERY PATCH OF SOIL WAS USED TO GROW SOMETHING USEFUL. Ask: which adjective describes land that yields a great deal? 'Empty' says the opposite; 'damp' only talks about water.
hints.S52_B1: Cover ON THE FARM and read what is left: EVERYONE. Ask: is that one person, or many? Words like everyone, nobody and someone take a singular verb - choose the form you would use after 'he' or 'she'.
hints.S52_B2: FOR OVER THIRTY YEARS means the selling began long ago and still goes on, and HAS is already there. Ask: which form must follow 'has'? This verb is irregular, so an -ed ending will not do.
hints.S52_B3: THAN LAST YEAR shows exactly two harvests being measured against each other. Ask: does a short adjective take -er, or 'the most'? A superlative is only for three or more, and 'smallish' is not exam English.
hints.S52_B4: THEIR FATHER CALLED THEM IN - a sudden event breaking into something already happening. Ask: which choice shows the children in the middle of their chore at that past moment? A plain past verb shows a finished job.
hints.S52_B5: Read the dash: NOT ENOUGH TO SELL AT THE MARKET, so the number is small. EGGS can be counted one by one. Ask: which quantity word goes with a countable plural and carries that 'not enough' feeling?
hints.S52_B6: The statement is positive, and its verb is CROWS - a plain present verb with no 'is' or 'are' in it. Ask: which helping verb stands in for it in the tag, and does a positive statement take a positive or a negative tag?
hints.S52_B7: The VEGETABLES did nothing - somebody carried them TO THE MARKET IN A COVERED TRUCK. Ask: which choice makes the subject the receiver of the action? And is that subject singular or plural?
hints.S52_B8: A reported command with a warning attached: OR THE SEEDLINGS WOULD DRY OUT. Ask: after 'told + person', is it the plain verb, the -ing form, or 'to' + verb? And does the negative word come before that little word, or after it?
hints.S52_C1: The clause names an age: HE WAS SEVEN YEARS OLD. Ask: which box word introduces a point or a period in the past? 'While' cannot take an age - 'while he was seven years old' is not English.
hints.S52_C2: Two people, two jobs, one stretch of time: FATHER MENDS the fence and MOTHER TENDS the vegetable patch side by side. Ask: which box word links two actions that run on together? A single-moment word will not do.
hints.S52_C3: Nobody can be sure of the weather, and the main clause says WE WILL HARVEST. Ask: which box word introduces something uncertain - a condition that may or may not come true? A time word would treat dry weather as certain.
hints.S52_C4: The clue is WITHOUT WASTING A SINGLE MINUTE - there is no gap at all between the milk being ready and the pouring. Ask: which box phrase means 'at the very moment that'? A plain time word would still allow a wait.
hints.S52_C5: The seedlings STAY UNDER THE SHADE NET and only leave it once they are STRONG ENOUGH. Ask: which box word means 'right up to that point in time'? 'Before' would end their shelter far too early.
hints.S52_C6: THE HENS ARE ALREADY PECKING HAPPILY BY THE TIME THE SCHOOL BUS ARRIVES, so the feeding must come first. Ask: which box word puts the chicken-feeding EARLIER than the leaving? Its opposite is needed in blank 7.
hints.S52_C7: The family can only celebrate once the crops are in: THE WHOLE FAMILY GATHERS TO SHARE A BIG MEAL. Ask: which box word puts the meal LATER than the harvest? It is the opposite of the word blank 6 needs.
hints.S52_C8: Read the ending: the animals come home EACH EVENING WITHOUT ANY HELP. A sudden STORM is the one thing that would stop them. Ask: which box word means 'except when'? The plain condition word would flip the meaning.
hints.S52_D1: The dash explains it: KNOWING WHEN TO PLANT, WATER AND GATHER CROPS - a repeating part of the year. Ask: which box word names that stretch of time? 'Harvest' is only the gathering at the end, not the whole cycle.
hints.S52_D2: The farmers take plants FROM TINY SEEDLINGS INTO HEALTHY PRODUCE with the right soil and water. The blank follows 'Farmers', so a verb is needed. Ask: which box word means to care for something so that it grows?
hints.S52_D3: The dash defines it: RICH IN NUTRIENTS TO SUPPORT HEALTHY ROOT GROWTH. The blank follows 'must be', so an adjective is needed. Ask: which box word describes soil that feeds plants well? 'Barren' means the exact opposite.
hints.S52_D4: The examples are listed for you: CHICKENS, COWS AND PIGS, kept FOR EGGS, MILK AND MEAT. Ask: which box word is the group name for farm animals? A 'scarecrow' is not an animal at all.
hints.S52_D5: AT THE END OF EACH GROWING CYCLE the farmer gathers ALL THE RIPE FRUITS AND VEGETABLES READY TO SELL. Ask: which box word names that gathering-in of ripe crops? A 'season' is a period of time, not the crops.
hints.S52_E1: The subject of the underlined verb is THE GOATS - more than one animal in the MEADOW. Ask: which past form of 'to be' belongs with a plural subject? Singular and plural never share the same form here.
hints.S52_E2: The underlined word sits in front of the verb WATER, and the sentence is not about 'also' or 'excessively'. Ask: which spelling marks an infinitive? The double-o spelling means 'as well' or 'more than enough'.
hints.S52_E3: The underlined word names the LARGE open ground BEHIND THE MAIN BARN, and its vowels are the wrong way round. Ask: with no C in front, which vowel leads - the I or the E? Compare: brief, believe, piece.
hints.S52_E4: Look at what the underlined word is describing: not the rooster, but the way it CROWED. Ask: which class of word may describe a verb - an adjective or an adverb? Build the manner word by adding -ly.
hints.S52_E5: The vegetables belong to ALL THREE FARMERS - the owners are more than one. Ask: a plain -s only makes a plural, so what must be added to show ownership, and on which side of the -s does that mark go?
hints.S52_F1: 'IF' opens the condition, so the sentence about the SOIL goes first. Ask: does a condition clause ever take 'will'? Keep the future verb for the second half, and separate the two halves with a comma.
hints.S52_F2: Both sentences name THE OLD BARN. Keep the one that says where it stood as the backbone, and slide the extra fact in straight after the barn. Ask: does 'which' still need 'it' after it, and where do the two commas go?
